public_notes.title: Roots Before A Modern Status Date
public_notes.text: The Tribe links its Northeast Alabama community to the lower Cherokee towns and cites documents from the 1700s and censuses from the 1800s. Its introduction dates formal state recognition to 1984. This is the Tribe's own account; the underlying historical records are not reproduced here. A modern status date is not the beginning of a people's history, and this community is not merged with other Cherokee governments.

public_notes.title: Constitution And District Representation
public_notes.text: The Tribe's government page dates a revision and ratification of its Constitution to June 6, 2006. It describes executive officers and a district-based Tribal Council, with constitutional amendments addressed at an annual meeting. These are its own published institutional descriptions. They do not establish the latest constitutional text, a reader's citizenship, authority to participate or a current legal remedy.
